answer: When an AI agent first registers, it must stake a tokenized proof of resource contribution, such as a verified timber‑supply contract recorded on a public ledger. Each subsequent identity the same entity creates receives a quadratic‑weight penalty: its influence scales as the square root of its stake, so a hundred dune‑size micro‑agents add less power than a single wharf‑level stake. An attacker therefore must acquire proportionally large real‑world assets to mount a Sybil attack, making the cost grow super‑linearly with the number of fake identities.
